data.title: Four States Ban Crypto Kiosks as Scams Cost Americans Nearly $389,000,000 in One Year
data.description:
Four states have banned cryptocurrency kiosks this year as scams tied to the machines cost Americans nearly $389 million in 2025.

The FBI says it received 13,460 complaints involving crypto kiosks in 2025.

Reported losses jumped 58% from the year before.

People older than 50 filed more than half of the complaints and reported over $302,000,000 in losses.

Indiana, Minnesota, Tennessee and Vermont have enacted statewide bans, reports Stateline.

Hawaii also barred consumers from depositing cash into kiosks to buy crypto under a law that took effect in October.

At least 20 Massachusetts communities have banned the machines as of August.

Jackson, Michigan and Star, Idaho, have passed bans of their own.

Attorneys general in Iowa, Massachusetts and the District of Columbia have sued kiosk operators.

They allege the operators failed to put adequate safeguards against fraud in place.

An Iowa attorney general investigation found that 98% of transactions at Bitcoin Depot kiosks in the state were linked to scams.

The figure was 94% at CoinFlip kiosks.

Bitcoin Depot has since filed for bankruptcy. It cited restrictive state regulations and bans. The company took its kiosks offline in May.

Operators have pushed back.

They argue the machines serve legitimate customers and that stronger fraud safeguards would better protect consumers than prohibitions.

Says Françoise Cleveland, AARP’s government affairs director,

“Every day that these laws aren’t passed are days where victims are having money stolen from them, and that money, because it’s through cryptocurrency and the nature of the kiosk, it’s just almost impossible to get any of that money back.”

data.title: DBS Teams Up With Circle to Give Asian Institutions 24/7 USDC Minting and Redemption
data.description:
A major Asian bank is partnering with a leading stablecoin issuer to give institutions direct round-the-clock access to minting and redeeming USDC.

DBS says the partnership expands institutional access to the stablecoin across Asia by enabling eligible clients to mint and redeem it through the bank.

The arrangement enables 24/7 USD-USDC settlement for seamless movement of value between fiat and digital environments.

Both firms are also participating in the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s Project BLOOM initiative to promote interoperability among tokenised money forms.

A DBS survey of 422 business leaders from firms with over USD 500 million in revenue across 11 markets found that 88% are already deploying or piloting tokenised money use cases.

Stablecoins lead adoption at 63%, followed by tokenised deposits and money market funds.

Over 60% of respondents are adopting or planning to adopt stablecoins, with expectations for benefits like improved auditability (72%) and real-time cross-border payments (71%).

Institutions are increasingly looking to tokenised money to manage liquidity more efficiently and support their growth across new markets.

“This partnership meets that demand by bringing together Circle’s regulated stablecoin infrastructure and global reach with DBS’ trusted banking, liquidity and digital asset capabilities in Asia.”

Financial institutions are increasingly looking for trusted ways to access stablecoins and integrate blockchain-based infrastructure into their financial operations.

“By combining Circle’s regulated stablecoin infrastructure with DBS’ institutional banking and liquidity capabilities, our partnership represents an important step in expanding institutional access to USDC across Asia, while strengthening the banking infrastructure supporting its global adoption.”

data.title: Florida Man Sentenced in North Carolina to 51 Months for $800,000 Cell Phone Tower Fraud Scheme
data.description:
Federal prosecutors have secured a 51-month prison sentence against a Florida man who ran a fraudulent cell phone tower consulting scheme that collected more than $800,000 from hundreds of victims.

Alexander Francise Blasscyk, 48, of Windermere, Florida, was sentenced in federal court in Charlotte, North Carolina, to 51 months in prison plus three years of supervised release and ordered to pay $1,039,115.30 in restitution, says the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of North Carolina.

According to court documents, Blasscyk defrauded victims by falsely claiming to be a cell tower consultant. Between 2018 and 2024, he told individuals, including residents of Ashe County, that he would market their properties to cell tower companies and wireless carriers for a fee. He also promised to negotiate lease agreements that would allow the companies to build towers on their land in exchange for rental payments.

Hundreds of victims, including individuals and businesses, paid Blasscyk or companies he controlled more than $800,000 for the purported consulting services and related expenses. However, little to no work was performed. Blasscyk did not market the properties to wireless carriers or cell tower companies as promised, nor did he negotiate the lease agreements he had offered to secure.

To persuade victims to hand over their money, Blasscyk provided false and fraudulent documents through his company.

Blasscyk used two companies to solicit fees for nonexistent work marketing land for tower leases and instead spent the money on personal expenses, including hotels, short-term rentals, restaurants and bars.

U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson said the defendant gave people the hope of passive income.

“Blasscyk gave people the hope of passive income — making false promises to lease land to cell phone tower companies while collecting consulting fees. But Blasscyk did no consulting, made no such deals, and created fake documents to cover up his fraud.”

He pleaded guilty to wire fraud in October 2025.

data.title: Investment Scams Cost Americans $27,500,000 in Eight Months, Topping Online Purchase Fraud
data.description:
Investment scams have cost Americans $27.5 million in reported losses over eight months, more than any other fraud type that commonly targets older adults.

Homewatch CareGivers says it analyzed Better Business Bureau Scam Tracker reports from January 1st to August 24th.

Online purchase fraud was the most reported scam, with 53,934 reports and $25 million in losses.

Phishing was second by volume, with 27,389 reports and $9 million in losses.

Investment scams ranked lower in volume, with 1,110 reports. Even so, their losses were the highest of any category in the study at $27.5 million.

“Although Online Purchase fraud and Phishing are the most commonly reported scams targeting seniors, Investment scams cost Americans more money. The Better Business Bureau tracked 1,110 Investment scams in our data period, and there were 15 types of scams that were more prevalent than this. But because of the high figures involved in investment scams, the total reported loss equals $27.5 million — three times the cost of Phishing to scam victims and dozens of times the cost of most other fraud types.”

Las Vegas had the highest rate of scams that commonly target seniors among 25 major cities, at 97 per 100,000 residents over an eight-month period.

Victims in Houston lost $1,009,000 to investment fraud, representing 9% of the total losses in the fraud category in Texas.

New Hampshire had the highest rate among states, with 816 reports, or 58 per 100,000 residents.

The figures include reports from victims of all ages, not just seniors.

data.title: Ransomware Gang Claims Visa and JPMorgan Chase as Victims, Sets 48-Hour Leak Deadline
data.description:
A newly emerged ransomware gang has listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase as alleged victims and threatens to leak stolen data within 48 hours.

The gang, which goes by the name n0n, has given the two companies 48 hours to negotiate, reports Cybernews.

Visa says it is aware of the claims and that the incident involved a third-party service provider in the Asia Pacific region.

Says a Visa spokesperson,

“Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. There is no indication that payment data such as card numbers have been affected.”

Visa has not said which third-party service providers were hit.

Meanwhile, JPMorgan Chase is separately dealing with a service outage that it blames on a software bug.

The bank says there is “no evidence” linking the disruption to a cyberattack.

The bank has not said whether the outage has any connection to the gang’s claims.

The n0n gang was first tracked in mid-September.

The gang claimed last week that it stole billions of traveler records from Expedia.

The attackers have offered few details about what they claim to have stolen from Visa and JPMorgan Chase.

The Daily HODL previously reported that JPMorgan Chase and other major US banks suffered a major outage that involved login failures and missing account balances.

data.title: Former Robinhood Engineer Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud Over Hyperliquid Insider Trades
data.description:
A former software engineer at a popular crypto trading app is pleading guilty to wire fraud after secretly using inside knowledge of upcoming token listings to trade derivatives on a decentralized platform.

The U.S. Department of Justice says Huaisong “Jerry” Xiang, 30, of Jersey City, New Jersey, worked on listing new digital assets and had access to nonpublic plans as a designated “Coin Aware Individual” via a private Slack channel.

Xiang repeatedly bought perpetual futures ahead of Robinhood’s public announcements between around March 2025 and February 2026 on Hyperliquid (HYPE), a decentralized platform for such contracts that do not expire.

“On each occasion, XIANG possessed material nonpublic information that Robinhood would list the cryptocurrency token on Robinhood Crypto, and XIANG traded on that information in breach of the duties that XIANG owed to Robinhood to maintain the confidentiality of this information.”

As part of the plea, he agreed to forfeit the full $125,523 in illicit profits, with sentencing set for February 25th, 2027, and a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.

Says US Attorney Jamie McDonald,

“No matter the trading platform, corporate insiders will be held accountable when they trade based on misappropriated information. As he has now admitted, Huaisong Xiang misused his employer’s confidential business information for his personal benefit. Over the course of a year, Xiang repeatedly traded in the derivatives market in advance of Robinhood’s public announcements.”

The case, handled by the SDNY Securities and Commodities Fraud Task Force with FBI assistance, highlights enforcement against insider trading even on decentralized crypto platforms.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway Sells 83.9% of Stake in One US Bank in Six Months While Trimming Bank of America by $1,500,000,000
data.description:
Billionaire Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway has sold most of its Capital One (COF) stake in just two quarters.

The conglomerate held 1,150,000 Capital One (COF) shares on September 30th, down from 7,150,000 on March 31st, reports Yahoo Finance.

Berkshire cut the stake to 3,000,000 COF shares in the second quarter, then to 1,150,000 in the third.

Over six months, 6,000,000 COF shares were sold, or 83.9% of the position.

The firm unloaded 1,850,000 COF shares in the third quarter, which were worth about $357 million at the September 30th price of $193.07.

The remaining shares were worth about $222 million, or 0.07% of the firm’s $304.20 billion portfolio, according to Berkshire’s latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Berkshire also trimmed Bank of America (BAC) by 5.7% in the third quarter to 455,860,908 BAC shares, a sale worth about $1.5 billion.

Meanwhile, the conglomerate’s American Express (AXP) stake did not change.

The 13F filing shows holdings as of September 30th and says nothing about trades since then.

Berkshire filed it on Monday, November 16th.

Greg Abel has run Berkshire as chief executive since the start of 2026, after Warren Buffett stepped down at the end of 2025.

The filing does not say who made each trade.

Capital One is a major US credit card issuer and bank.

data.title: Hacker Exploits Trader on Ethereum DEX Lighter, Looting $10,000,000 Worth of Crypto
data.description:
A hacker looted $10 million worth of crypto from a trader operating on the Ethereum (ETH) decentralized exchange Lighter.

The blockchain security firm PeckShield published an alert about the hack early Monday morning, noting the hacker had already bridged 640 ETH, worth $1.12 million, to Hyperliquid to buy 2,240 Monero (XMR), a privacy coin.

Lighter temporarily suspended withdrawals to investigate the exploit, then resumed them several hours later. The project noted the incident was caused by a leaked API key for a specific trader’s account and didn’t impact its trading protocol, smart contracts or infrastructure.

“Every transaction on Lighter is authorized by a signature from an API key. Each signature uses a one-off random value called a nonce, which must be unique and unpredictable every time.

Signatures are public. If the same nonce is used with the same key to sign two different transactions, anyone can calculate the private key from those two signatures. After that, the key is exposed, and needs to be rotated.

This issue isn’t specific to Lighter – the above applies to Bitcoin and Ethereum signatures as well.”

Lighter’s native token, LIT, is trading at $2.74 at time of writing. The 86th-ranked crypto asset by market cap is down more than 3% in the past day and more than 17% in the past week, per data from CoinGecko.

data.title: Bitmine Adds 7,653 ETH Worth $14,000,000 Amid Sharp Selloff
data.description:
A major Ethereum treasury firm is continuing to buy the ETH token during a steep selloff.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies has just added 7,653 ETH.

The purchases bring its total holdings to 6,077,745 ETH valued at roughly $11.1 billion at $1,823 per token.

The company now controls 4.97% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply.

Bitmine holds $11.8 billion overall in crypto, cash, marketable securities, and other assets, including $448 million in cash and securities plus stakes in other firms.

Chairman Tom Lee says the 28% decline over two weeks and 39% over eight weeks does not match positive fundamentals like bank tokenization projects on Ethereum.

“ETH tumbled 28% in the past two weeks. This waterfall decline in price is not consistent with what we view as the relatively positive cadence of fundamental developments, including multiple financial institutions and banks announcing tokenization projects built on Ethereum.”

Lee points to Nvidia-related margin selling and investors raising cash before the Anthropic IPO planned for November 18, 2026, as key factors.

“In our view, external factors could be weighing on ETH prices including the recent developments on Nvidia (triggering margin selling, particularly in Asia) and also the upcoming Anthropic IPO (planned pricing is reported to be November 18, 2026), as investors raise cash ahead of the sizable equity offering.”

Lee notes the pattern mirrors Ethereum’s 29% drop in the two weeks before the $75 billion SpaceX IPO in June 2026.

“Over the past week, we acquired 7,653 ETH. Bitmine’s track record of consistent buying of crypto is unmatched by any public company in the world. Bitmine has bought ETH each week since the inception of the ETH Treasury Strategy on June 30, 2025.”

The firm has purchased ETH weekly since launching its treasury strategy in June 2025 and now stakes over 5.2 million ETH through its MAVAN platform.

Ethereum is trading for $1,828 at time of writing, down more than 14% in the past seven days.

data.title: Visa and Mastercard Urge Federal Judge To Approve $38,000,000,000 Swipe Fee Settlement
data.description:
Merchants could soon pay lower card fees and gain the right to refuse certain credit cards under a $38 billion settlement now before a federal judge.

Visa and Mastercard urged a judge on Monday to approve the deal, reports Reuters.

The agreement would end claims that the card networks charged merchants excessive fees to process credit card payments.

The settlement would cut the average swipe fee by 0.1 percentage point for five years and cap fees on standard consumer cards at 1.25% for eight years.

It would also end the Honor All Cards rule, which requires merchants to accept all Visa and Mastercard cards or none.

Merchants could instead choose whether to accept commercial cards, premium consumer cards or standard consumer cards.

Visa says the deal would also give merchants more options to surcharge and add a new merchant education program.

Visa’s lawyer Michael Shuster says that the settlement provides “potent” relief for merchants, while the card network is not “jumping with joy.”

“It’s going to change life for the [card] networks.”

U.S. District Judge Brian Cogan in Brooklyn did not rule at the hearing, but said rejecting the settlement could lead to a protracted process in the 21-year-old case.

Cogan granted preliminary approval in June, and a different judge rejected an earlier $30 billion version in 2024.
